newsitem.title: CANADA: BASEBALL-O'S ALOMAR SUSPENDED, APPEALS, HITS CLINCHING HOME RUN.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-O'S ALOMAR SUSPENDED, APPEALS, HITS CLINCHING HOME RUN.

text.p: Baltimore Orioles All-Star second baseman Roberto Alomar had quite an eventful day Saturday.

Alomar was handed a five-game suspension, appealed, was verbally attacked in the locker room by an umpire, then went out and hit the 10th-inning, game-winning home run against his former team that lifted his current team into the playoffs.
Alomar's homer gave the Orioles a 3-2 victory over the Toronto Blue Jays and clinched the American League wild card for Baltimore.
The Orioles secured their first post-season berth since 1983, when they won the World Series against the Philadelphia Phillies.
Alomar was suspended for five regular-season games for bumping and spitting in the face of home plate umpire John Hirschbeck while protesting a call in Friday night's game at Toronto.
American League President Gene Budig swiftly handed out the suspension Saturday, which was for Baltimore's final two regular-season games this weekend and first three games next season.
But Alomar officially appealed the suspension with the Orioles vying for the wild card,and then came through with the big blow off his first pitch from reliever Paul Spoljaric.
After the game, Alomar had to explain both his heroics and his spat with Hirschbeck.
"I am not happy about what happened, but we are just human and we both made mistakes," Alomar said. "I will try to talk to him when I get a chance.
He added: "Today was a great way to put it behind me. As long as we win, that's what matters. I had the chance to be in a situation to get a big hit."

And there was a little revenge factor, too. "To get the win here in Toronto, the way they were battling back, makes it sweeter," said Alomar, a mainstay of Toronto's 1992 and 1993 World Series winners.

Alomar was ejected in the first inning Friday by Hirschbeck for arguing balls and strikes. The argument escalated and Alomar had to be restrained by manager Davey Johnson after bumping into Hirschbeck.

"What's there to regret? I don't regret nothing I did," Alomar said Friday. "It's one in a million, he caught me in a bad moment. It's the first time I reacted that way. I was yelling, but I kind of spat at him, too. I don't think he should've thrown me out of the game in a game like this."
Alomar also said that Hirschbeck has become "more bitter" because of personal problems.

"I don't have nothing against him, I used to respect him a lot," said Alomar. "But he had problems with his family, his son died. That's tough for anyone. But he changed personality-wise, he got more bitter."

Hirschbeck became angered when he learned of Alomar's post-game comments Saturday morning. He ran into the Orioles' locker room and was yelling at Alomar before he was led away from the clubhouse by a fellow umpire.
As a result, Hirschbeck, who was slated to umpire third base, did not work in Saturday's game.
Baltimore will host the first two games of the best-of-five division series against the Central Division champion Cleveland Indians starting Tuesday.
Baltimore's win officially eliminated the Chicago White Sox and Seattle Mariners from the wild-card race.
